title: Every Popcorn Kernel Is a Pressure Cooker #science #physics
description:
Every popcorn kernel is a tiny pressure cooker. Inside is a little water (about 14 % of the kernel) sealed in a hard hull. Heated near 180 °C, the pressure inside reaches about 10 times the air around it, the hull bursts, and the starch puffs into a foam. And the pop? Most likely the sound of the steam escaping, according to the researchers who filmed it.

More kitchen physics: Why microwaves don't heat food from the inside https://youtu.be/ri17BZl0Iq8

Sources
- Virot, E. & Ponomarenko, A. (2015), Popcorn: critical temperature, jump and sound, Journal of the Royal Society Interface 12: 20141247
- Hoseney, R. C., Zeleznak, K. & Abdelrahman, A. (1983), Mechanism of popcorn popping, Journal of Cereal Science 1: 43–52

Butter or salt on your popcorn?
